answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral, so coordinated equivocation by k identities creates up to k(k−1)/2 penalized pairs and O(k²) slashing exposure. Detection also triggers asymmetric depreciation: losses compound across the swarm, producing an exponential multiplier in capital destroyed rather than a cheap per-identity fee. Like nectar spread across an ocean, divided stake offers no shelter when the tide of correlated evidence arrives.
